concepts.title: Classification of Plants by Growth Habit

questions.q: How are plants classified by how they stand?
questions.a: As herbs (soft, small), shrubs (bushy, woody near base) and trees (tall, hard trunk).

questions.q: Give two examples each of herbs, shrubs and trees.
questions.a: Herbs: spinach, tomato. Shrubs: hibiscus, lemon. Trees: mango, neem.

questions.q: What are creepers and climbers?
questions.a: Plants with weak stems - creepers spread on ground (pumpkin); climbers climb with support (grape vine).

questions.q: Why do creepers and climbers have weak stems?
questions.a: They cannot stand upright on their own, so they spread or climb for support.

questions.q: Name a climber and its climbing organ.
questions.a: Grape vine (or money plant) climbs using tendrils or twisting stems.

questions.q: How does a pumpkin plant spread?
questions.a: As a creeper, its weak stem trails along the ground.

questions.q: Name the functions of a stem.
questions.a: It holds branches and leaves up, carries water and minerals upward, and carries food from leaves.

questions.q: How does a cactus stem help the plant?
questions.a: It is green and fleshy - makes food and stores water in place of leaves.

questions.q: What shows that water travels through the stem?
questions.a: A white flower kept in coloured water turns coloured - water rose through the stem.

questions.q: Name the main parts of a leaf.
questions.a: Petiole (stalk), lamina (flat blade), midrib and veins.

questions.q: What is the network of veins in a leaf called?
questions.a: Venation - reticulate (net-like) or parallel.

questions.q: What is the green flat part of a leaf called?
questions.a: The lamina (leaf blade).

questions.q: What is reticulate venation? Give an example.
questions.a: A net-like vein pattern - mango, peepal, hibiscus leaves.

questions.q: What is parallel venation? Give an example.
questions.a: Veins running side by side - grass, wheat, banana leaves.

questions.q: How does venation help classify plants?
questions.a: It is a visible character - dicots show reticulate, monocots parallel venation.

questions.q: What is transpiration?
questions.a: Escape of water vapour from the leaf surface, mostly through stomata.

questions.q: How does transpiration help the plant?
questions.a: It cools the plant and pulls water up from the roots.

questions.q: How can you see transpiration at home?
questions.a: Cover a potted plant with a polybag - water drops collect inside overnight.

questions.q: What is photosynthesis?
questions.a: Green leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food and release oxygen.

questions.q: Why are leaves called the food factories of plants?
questions.a: Chlorophyll in leaves captures sunlight and prepares the plant's food there.

questions.q: Write the raw materials and products of photosynthesis.
questions.a: Raw: CO2 and water. Products: glucose and oxygen.

questions.q: What is a taproot system? Give examples.
questions.a: One main root going deep with smaller side roots - mustard, carrot, mango.

questions.q: What is a fibrous root system? Give examples.
questions.a: A bunch of thin similar roots from the stem base - wheat, grass, onion.

questions.q: Which root system do dicot and monocot plants show?
questions.a: Dicots: taproot. Monocots: fibrous roots.

questions.q: What link exists between root type and leaf venation?
questions.a: Taproot plants show reticulate venation; fibrous-root plants show parallel venation.

questions.q: A plant has parallel venation - what roots would you expect?
questions.a: A fibrous root system (as in grasses).

questions.q: Why do plants with reticulate venation usually have taproots?
questions.a: They are dicots - their embryo and organs develop in the matching pattern.

questions.q: Name the outer parts of a flower.
questions.a: Sepals (green, protect the bud) and petals (coloured, attract insects).

questions.q: What is the function of sepals?
questions.a: They enclose and protect the flower bud before it opens.

questions.q: Why are petals colourful and scented?
questions.a: To attract insects for pollination.

questions.q: Name the male and female reproductive parts of a flower.
questions.a: Stamen (male - makes pollen) and pistil (female - holds ovules).

questions.q: What does a stamen contain?
questions.a: A filament bearing the anther, which makes pollen grains.

questions.q: What does the pistil consist of?
questions.a: Stigma (receives pollen), style (tube) and ovary (holds ovules).

questions.q: What is the ovary of a flower?
questions.a: The lower part of the pistil that holds one or many ovules.

questions.q: What do ovules become after fertilisation?
questions.a: They mature into seeds.

questions.q: What does the ovary ripen into?
questions.a: The fruit, which surrounds the seeds.
